question: Twenty-two runs/*/levels.jsonl are zero bytes and inner/levels.py exists in full. Is the detector never called, called and never firing, or firing and never writing?
answer: Called on every recorded step, never fired, and -- for every case but one -- it writes correctly when it does fire. The exception is the winning increment, which it was coded never to record at all.

spend.network: none. Every leg below ran offline against proxy/mock over a loopback socket; no credential was read.

2_why_the_live_legs_are_empty.verdict: the counter never moved in front of the arm
2_why_the_live_legs_are_empty.evidence: A34's own arithmetic: g50t level 1 costs a reference solver 78 actions (runs/20260728T015354Z-g50t-first-contact/run.json, [78, 175, 179, 230, 96, 54, 67]); the longest theoria-arm leg walked 33 and spent 28 of them on probes.

sweep.reading: 11 of 30 legs carry a readable completion record and they sum to 0. The other 19 are not zeros: no envelope in them ever carried levels_completed, so nothing looked.

2_why_the_live_legs_are_empty.note_on_the_19: unmeasured is not a defect claim. It covers legs that died before their first successful command, legs written before the field was captured in trace.jsonl, and the two A26b legs that were still in flight when this was measured (their trace.jsonl is written at _save_all, so a running leg reads as unmeasured by construction). No conclusion about A26b is drawn here.

3_why_the_mock_legs_are_empty.verdict: the default offline explorer provably cannot reach the mock's goal, at any budget
3_why_the_mock_legs_are_empty.policy: inner/loop._probe_or_explore, no-manual branch: chosen = min(legal, key=lambda a: (action_counts[a], a)) -- the least-tried legal action, ties to the lowest id. offline=True makes no model call, so there is never a manual, so this is the only branch reachable.
3_why_the_mock_legs_are_empty.consequence: runs/a3-gate-mock/levels.jsonl and runs/audit-smoke/levels.jsonl being zero bytes was never evidence that the recording path was broken -- and never evidence that it worked. It was a fact about the explorer. This is the lead A34 called strongest, and it is the one that dissolves.

4_the_positive_control_that_was_missing.before: every test of the boundary in tests/test_levels.py drives TheoriaArm._record directly with a hand-built envelope. That proves the unit. The twenty-two empty files were written by the shell.
4_the_positive_control_that_was_missing.built: tests/test_levels_recording_path.py -- harness.run.play, the real env proxy, the real proxy/mock world, and a scripted walk (derived by BFS over the mock's own Session at test time, never a hand-copied constant) that genuinely reaches the goal.

result.row: level_boundary, signal levels_completed, from_level 1 -> to_level 2, step_idx 13, witnessed true
result.turns_json: one row with beat 'level', detail 'level 1 complete'

4_the_positive_control_that_was_missing.verdict: the boundary path works end to end. It had simply never been asked.

5_the_defect_the_positive_control_found.before: on a synthetic 3-level game won in three increments, LevelLog recorded 2 events and levels.jsonl 2 rows, while inner/scoreboard.ScoreWatch recorded 3 level_boundary events and reported verdict 'observed'. witnessed_wins.json held 2 witnesses. The row that was missing was the win.
5_the_defect_the_positive_control_found.scaled_up: a seven-level g50t win would have written six rows to levels.jsonl and left the seventh -- the win itself, the single most important event this project can observe -- off disk, while the second instrument recorded all seven.
5_the_defect_the_positive_control_found.why_it_was_there: the suppression is correct for the DESTRUCTIVE half of the handling: _on_level_boundary drops problem.json and wipes generated/, which on a winning run deletes exactly the artefacts that say how it was won (test_winning_the_last_level_does_not_open_an_eighth pins this). The argument covered the handling and was silently extended to the record, which it never covered.

6_do_the_two_instruments_agree.question: A27 landed inner/scoreboard.py with a default-on envelope rung. Two detectors for one event is worse than one if they can disagree silently.
6_do_the_two_instruments_agree.found: they contradicted each other on exactly one input -- the winning increment -- and nothing in either instrument could say so. ScoreWatch.corroborate() compares the envelope counter against a SCORECARD reading; it never compares ScoreWatch's own event list against LevelLog's. On a won game the arm would have reported boundary_observed: true with a levels.jsonl short by one row and no verdict of 'disagree' anywhere.
6_do_the_two_instruments_agree.now: every increment ScoreWatch sees has a row in levels.jsonl. summary() keeps the two kinds apart -- boundaries (segmenting, paired with starts) and game_won (not) -- rather than adding them into one number, and the test asserts boundaries + game_won == the free rung's event count.
6_do_the_two_instruments_agree.still_open: the two instruments are still reconciled only by a test, not by a runtime check. A disagreement introduced later would be caught by tests/test_levels_recording_path.py and by nothing in a live leg.

6b_the_downstream_defect_the_fix_exposed.problem: `boundaries` counts SEGMENTING boundaries -- the ones with a level after them. The increment that finishes the game is not one, by construction. So a leg that WON its game counted zero completions: it contributed nothing to the campaign's levels_completed, and `_progress` called the winning leg unproductive, which means a three-leg zero-progress streak could have stopped the campaign immediately after the only win in the project's history.
6b_the_downstream_defect_the_fix_exposed.found_by: fixing the upstream defect. Before this ticket `boundaries` also excluded the win, so the two sites were already wrong and nothing could show it -- there was no `game_won` to count.
6b_the_downstream_defect_the_fix_exposed.fix: harness.campaign._completions = boundaries + game_won, used at both sites; `legs_with_no_level_record` added so a leg with no levels block at all is counted rather than summed as 0; campaign_series marks the winning turn by reading events + finals.
6b_the_downstream_defect_the_fix_exposed.honest_note: nothing had ever won, so nothing had ever been wrong. That is not the same as being right.

7_the_negative_control.asked_for_by: A34's closing section: build a mock leg that DID complete a level, truncate its levels.jsonl to zero bytes, and require every instrument to report 'completion information missing' rather than zero completions.
7_the_negative_control.before: armtools/round.py:188 read sum((l.get('levels_completed') or 0) for l in legs). Under that rule a leg that completed a level and lost its record contributed exactly what a leg that completed nothing contributed. A31 proved the `or 0`; this is the case that makes it bite.
7_the_negative_control.now: armtools/level_evidence.py returns levels_completed: None for evidence_missing and for unmeasured, and total() sums only the legs whose artefacts support a count while naming the rest. round.json's totals carry a `levels` block instead of an integer.

the_five_verdicts.observed: levels.jsonl carries rows; the count is a number
the_five_verdicts.measured_absent: the counter was read and never rose; 0 is honest here and ONLY here
the_five_verdicts.unmeasured: no envelope carried the counter; None
the_five_verdicts.evidence_missing: a source says a level was completed and levels.jsonl has no row for it; None, never the number

8_is_the_fix_exercised_on_a_real_positiv.answer: No. Zero archived legs contain a real boundary.
8_is_the_fix_exercised_on_a_real_positiv.evidence: the sweep in section 2: 30 leg directories, 0 observed, 0 evidence_missing. 11 legs looked at the counter across every envelope and it never rose; 19 never looked. The same claim from the other side is pinned by A27's test_no_recorded_leg_contains_a_real_boundary, over 2,700 env_step rows and 47 recoverable scorecards.
8_is_the_fix_exercised_on_a_real_positiv.consequence: every positive in this run is synthetic or mock. The fix is unexercised on real positives and that is the honest status. What changed is that the instrument is now known to fire and known to write, so the next 'no boundary' is a measurement instead of an unfalsifiable sentence.
8_is_the_fix_exercised_on_a_real_positiv.what_would_change_it: the first live leg that increments levels_completed. A34's own ordering says that is step 2 or 3 (a 78-action bare_cc run, or the A26b long leg re-read against this result), and neither is this item's to spend.

negative_controls: a leg that completed a level, with levels.jsonl truncated to zero bytes, reads as evidence_missing with levels_completed None -- not 0, and not 1
the same leg, aggregated with a genuine zero and a leg that never looked, produces legs_counted 1 of 3 and names the other two rather than summing them
a leg with 4 envelopes carrying the counter and no increase reads measured_absent with levels_completed 0 -- the one place a zero is honest
a leg whose only trace row is a failed command reads unmeasured with levels_completed None
the default offline explorer over 200 mock actions: 2 distinct positions, 0 completions -- absence of a completion is absence of a reachable goal, recorded as such
the destructive half of the boundary handler is still refused at a win: problem.json survives, generated/ survives, starts is not cut, and levels.level does not become 4 in a 3-level game

the pre-fix code was re-run under the new tests (git stash of inner/) and test_the_two_instruments_agree_about_the_winning_increment failed with '2 rows reached disk; the missing one is the win'. The test is red without the fix.
residual_gaps: unexercised on a real positive -- see section 8

the win path's `_on_game_won` has never run against a live API. It is exercised only through hand-built envelopes with win_levels set, because proxy/mock never returns win_levels at all, so no mock leg can reach the final_level branch.
LevelLog and ScoreWatch are reconciled by a test, not at runtime. A future divergence is caught in pytest and nowhere in a leg.

level_evidence reads trace.jsonl, which is written at _save_all. A leg killed before that reads as unmeasured even if its ledger holds the increment. The ledger is the stronger source and is not consulted here.
armtools/round.py's totals block changed shape (levels_completed integer -> levels object). No round.json on disk was rewritten; older files keep the old key.
